title: Innkeeping software user and role report
what_it_shows: One user account, the administrator account in the owner's name, created when the software was adopted in 2019; the administrator role includes the permission to display full card numbers; a front desk role and other roles exist with no users assigned; no record of a user list review

title: Innkeeping software sign-in and security settings
what_it_shows: Password sign-in; two-step verification is available and turned off for the administrator account; session and lockout settings are set by the vendor; the booking engine, channel manager for the two OTAs, guest messaging and the door code integration are turned on

title: Innkeeping software activity log and export history
what_it_shows: The activity log records sign-ins, full card number displays, exports and setting changes for every user and covers the last 12 months; it shows full card number displays on OTA virtual cards about once a month; the export history shows no data export since 2019; no record of a log review

title: Guest register and guest profile report, 12 months to 2026-06-30
what_it_shows: Chronological guest register with dates of occupancy and rates, kept electronically since 2019; about 600 stays and about 1,100 room-nights in the 12 months (about 50% occupancy of six rooms); average daily rate about $155 with breakfast included; about 3,400 guest profiles created since 2019; about 55% of guests give a Florida address and most others an address in another state

title: Booking engine and website payment path check
what_it_shows: The website's booking button links to a booking and payment page on the innkeeping vendor's own web address; the website hosts no payment form; online reservations show a payment token and the last 4 digits of the card; the booking engine's room list shows nightly rates, and the $15 housekeeping fee is added on the final payment step, where taxes and the final amount are shown before payment

title: Website rate table, privacy statement and chat widget
what_it_shows: The rate table lists nightly rates with no housekeeping fee; the privacy statement says "we never store your card details"; the AI chat assistant from the innkeeping add-on (SYS-11) appears on every page; contact form messages go to the owner's email

title: Payment facilitator portal: compliance status, fees and devices
what_it_shows: Sub-merchant account in the owner's name, integrated with the innkeeping software; the compliance section shows no self-assessment questionnaire submitted since the account opened; monthly statements show a $19.95 PCI non-compliance fee each month since March 2024; one Bluetooth mobile reader registered, described in the facilitator's documentation as part of a PCI-listed validated P2PE solution; pay-by-link is available and has never been used; card receipts show only the last 4 digits

title: Payment facilitator transaction report by entry method, 12 months to 2026-06-30
what_it_shows: About 1,050 card transactions totalling about $165,000: about 420 booking engine deposits, about 160 OTA virtual cards charged through the innkeeping software, about 120 phone payments keyed in the innkeeping payment screen, and about 350 card-present payments on the mobile reader; about $3,200 of card payments a week on average

title: Sub-merchant agreement, current version
what_it_shows: Fictional terms: the inn must comply with PCI DSS, validate every year by self-assessment questionnaire in the facilitator's compliance portal, and notify the facilitator within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise; a monthly fee applies while validation is outstanding

title: OTA partner portal security and user settings (OTA-1 and OTA-2)
what_it_shows: OTA-1: one login in the owner's name; a sign-in code is sent to the owner's phone. OTA-2: one login in the owner's name; password only, with sign-in verification available and turned off; both portals display full virtual card numbers on reservations and offer user roles, and only the owner's login is in use

title: Email and file account security page and settings
what_it_shows: Personal consumer plan in the owner's name used for the inn; password sign-in, with two-step verification available and turned off; the provider keeps a sign-in history; provider spam filtering is on; photo backup from the phone is on; no file version history on this plan; the inbox holds card authorization forms emailed by guests and third-party payers such as wedding parties and parents

title: Mailbox search for card numbers
what_it_shows: A search for card authorization forms and card-number patterns returned about 85 emails with card numbers from 2022 to July 2026, 31 of which include security codes; the messages were counted, not opened in full

title: Laptop settings review
what_it_shows: One user profile with a password that family members also use; family personal browsing and games on the same profile; automatic updates on and update history current; built-in antivirus on with real-time protection; host firewall on; time set automatically; full-disk encryption off; screen lock after 20 minutes; no backup configured; contracts, receipts, tax documents and downloaded guest reports in local folders; phone payments are keyed in the innkeeping payment screen in the browser; the IT consultant's remote-support tool is installed

title: Laptop browser saved-password list
what_it_shows: 18 passwords saved in the browser, including those for the innkeeping software, email and both OTA portals; the browser's password check lists one password used for both the innkeeping software and email and several passwords under 10 characters

title: Mobile phone settings and content review
what_it_shows: Passcode set; locks after 30 seconds; device encryption on; automatic updates on; time set automatically; the payment app is paired with the mobile reader; innkeeping, OTA and email apps installed; receives the sign-in codes for OTA-1 and the accounting SaaS; the camera roll holds about 1,900 photos of guests' driver licenses and passports taken at check-in since 2021, synced to the consumer photo backup, with no deletion setting; guest text threads

title: Router status page
what_it_shows: One Wi-Fi network with WPA2 serves guests and the owner's laptop and phone, with one password that is printed on a card in every guest room; the router's guest network feature is available and turned off; the router blocks unsolicited inbound traffic; the firmware version is the one installed by the internet service provider, with no update recorded

title: Smart lock app settings and code history
what_it_shows: Keypads on the front door and 6 guest rooms; per-reservation random 6-digit codes are sent by the innkeeping integration and expire at checkout; one house master code used by the owner, the relief innkeeper and the cleaners, last changed in 2022

title: Owner's office review
what_it_shows: The office holds the laptop, the mobile reader, the paper reservation pad and a binder of printed card authorization forms; the office door is not locked during the day while guests and cleaners are in the house; the cleaners do not clean the office; about 140 pad pages since 2023, with card numbers and security codes, in an unlocked desk drawer; a home cross-cut shredder is used for paper; mechanical override keys for the door locks are kept in a lockbox; the weekly arrivals list printed for the cleaners is shredded each week

title: Search of the owner's files for security documents
source_system: Laptop; email and file account; paper files
what_it_shows: No written security policy, procedure, risk assessment, incident plan, contact list, card data flow list or PCI DSS scope document, retention rule, settings record, component list, provider list, acceptable use rule, or training record was found; no prior SAQ or attestation of compliance was found

title: Owner's written intake answers
what_it_shows: Phone bookings are keyed in the innkeeping payment screen on the laptop or, away from the laptop, written on the paper pad with the security code and keyed later; third-party payers email card authorization forms; the owner displays full OTA virtual card numbers about once a month to check a declined card; the owner and relief innkeeper quote nightly rates by phone without the housekeeping fee; the owner photographs every guest's driver license or passport at check-in; the router administrator password is the one printed on the device label and the firmware has never been updated; the owner has had no security training; the owner had not read the facilitator's 24-hour notice term and believed the vendors covered PCI DSS

title: Relief innkeeper's intake answers
source_system: Relief innkeeper (written answers collected by the owner)
what_it_shows: Covers about two weekends a month and the owner's days off: check-ins, phone bookings and breakfast; signs in to the innkeeping software and OTA-2 with the owner's username and password; uses the house master door code; has no account of their own in any system

title: Cleaning service agreement and correspondence
what_it_shows: Two cleaners turn rooms daily and enter with the house master door code; the agreement gives them no access to any system and says nothing about screening; a 2024 email from the cleaning service reports that one cleaner left the service

title: Accounting SaaS users and security settings; bookkeeper engagement letter
source_system: Accounting SaaS admin settings (SYS-05); signed agreements folder
what_it_shows: The vendor enforces MFA for every user; two users, the owner and the bookkeeper's named user; payout and bank records with no card numbers; the engagement letter covers monthly bookkeeping and the Florida sales and tourist development tax returns

title: Bank and card statements, 2025-07-01 to 2026-07-12
source_system: Business bank account and card statements
what_it_shows: Deposits are mainly payment facilitator payouts; recurring payments to the innkeeping software vendor, the consumer email and file plan, the accounting SaaS, the website builder, the smart lock vendor, the internet service provider, the phone carrier, the cleaning service, the bookkeeper and the business owner's insurer; hourly payments to the IT consultant; no payment for a standalone cyber insurance policy

title: 2025 Schedule C (Form 1040)
what_it_shows: Gross receipts of about $180,000; no wages paid; the business is a sole proprietorship with no employees

title: Business owner's insurance policy declarations
what_it_shows: Business owner's policy in force for 2026; the declarations page does not list a data breach or cyber endorsement; the full policy form was requested from the agent

title: IT consultant confidentiality agreement
what_it_shows: Signed 2026-07-17; covers inn and guest information; hourly help with the laptop, router and door locks; remote sessions only when the owner starts them; no standing access to any system

title: AI add-on settings
what_it_shows: The AI add-on was turned on 2026-05-01 with two features, rate suggestions and the website chat assistant; rate suggestions are set to apply automatically to the calendar, booking engine and both OTA channels; the floor, ceiling and daily change limit fields are blank; there is no setting for a declared state of emergency; the chat assistant answers questions and quotes rates and availability, then links to the booking engine

title: AI chat transcript screen
what_it_shows: Transcripts since 2026-05-01 are listed with guests' names and emails and no deletion date; chat answers about rates quote nightly rates with no housekeeping fee; some guest messages contain card numbers (not counted at intake)

title: Innkeeping vendor SOC 2 Type 2 report
what_it_shows: Type 2 report with an unqualified opinion on the Security and Availability categories for the 12 months ending 2026-03-31; one exception, a missed quarterly access review of vendor support staff, remediated; the system description states RTO 4 hours and RPO 1 hour, an annual recovery test, encrypted backups with integrity checks kept in a separate location, and an activity log kept 12 months; the hosting provider is a carved-out subservice organization; lists complementary user entity controls; the AI add-on launched after the period and is outside the report's scope

title: Innkeeping vendor PCI DSS attestation of compliance (service provider)
what_it_shows: Service provider attestation of compliance for the innkeeping platform, including its card vault and the hosted booking and payment page

title: Payment facilitator PCI DSS attestation of compliance (service provider)
what_it_shows: Service provider attestation of compliance for processing, the card vault and pay-by-link

title: BIA self-review worksheet
source_system: Owner-innkeeper's written BIA worksheet, reviewed with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: For each of the five business functions, the owner's account of the systems and vendors used, the manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss the function can tolerate; the owner holds every password, receives every sign-in code and deals with every vendor; no relocation arrangement with another inn exists; the relief innkeeper is the natural backup operator; the inn is a single coastal property and hurricane season runs June to November

title: Risk walk-through of the house, devices and accounts
source_system: Walk-through of the house, the office desk drawer, the laptop, the phone, the router and each SaaS account with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: The router client list shows guests' devices and the laptop on one network; the router settings were viewed; the unlocked desk drawer holds about 140 pad pages and the binder of card forms; about 1,900 guest ID photos counted on the phone; where card data enters day to day (pad, email forms, keyed entry on the laptop, displayed virtual cards); after the walk-through the owner stopped writing new card numbers on the pad, and existing pages remain

title: Gap analysis self-review (PCI DSS)
source_system: Owner-innkeeper's written answers to the PCI DSS questions, checked on screen with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: No written procedures for any of the 12 PCI DSS requirement areas; setting changes are made as needed with no record; nobody checks that antivirus or logging keeps running; no wireless access point check, vulnerability scan, penetration test, or intrusion or file-change detection has been run; the laptop is used on other networks when travelling; the inn does not screen the cleaners; the relief innkeeper is a family member

title: P2PE solution listing check
source_system: PCI SSC website (list of validated P2PE solutions); facilitator's P2PE Instruction Manual
what_it_shows: The facilitator's P2PE solution used by the mobile reader appears on the PCI SSC list of validated P2PE solutions; the P2PE Instruction Manual describes device inspection and serial number checks

title: Mailbox search with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: The intake search re-run with the IT consultant returned about 85 emails with card numbers from 2022 to July 2026, 31 with security codes; messages were counted, not opened in full

title: Fee display screenshots
source_system: Inn website (SYS-06); booking engine (SYS-01); OTA-2 listing
what_it_shows: The website rate table and the booking engine room list show nightly rates only; the booking engine adds the $15 fee at the final payment step, calls it a "housekeeping fee", and shows taxes and the final amount before payment; phone booking confirmations show the final amount; the OTA-2 listing shows the fee separately as a "resort fee"

title: Mobile reader serial number record
source_system: Mobile reader label; owner's device record
what_it_shows: The serial number of the one P2PE mobile reader was written down for the first time; no inspection record for the reader exists

title: Payment facilitator email on the 2026 SAQ type
what_it_shows: Fictional: the facilitator accepts validation for 2026 on SAQ A plus SAQ P2PE once phone payments move to pay-by-link, the pad and email forms are destroyed, and virtual cards are charged without display; attestations due 2026-12-31

title: AI add-on terms, as read
what_it_shows: Rate suggestions use the inn's own booking history and public OTA rates; the inn's non-public data is not shared with other inns; chat transcripts are kept with no deletion period; the add-on has no personalized pricing feature

title: AI rate change log, May to August 2026
what_it_shows: 214 automatic rate changes from May to August 2026; the highest applied rate was $289 on a festival weekend; no declared state of emergency covered the county in the period

title: Chat assistant test and transcript search
what_it_shows: 20 test questions: 18 answered correctly, with the pet fee and the cancellation window wrong; 0 of the 8 rate answers included the $15 fee; 4 transcripts contain card numbers

title: Control assessment: Log review self-review
source_system: Innkeeping activity log screen; email sign-in history; OTA-2 login history; lock app access log; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The activity log screen was viewed with the IT consultant; none of the four logs has ever been reviewed; no process exists to act on what a review finds or to review more often after an incident or a vendor warning

title: Control assessment: Router and lock settings test
source_system: Router settings; lock app settings; laptop and phone settings
what_it_shows: No settings are documented for the router, locks, laptop or phone, and no deviations or approvals are recorded; the router uses the default administrator password, had internet-side remote management turned on (the IT consultant turned it off the same day) and has no guest network; router and lock app setting changes are not monitored; the router's administrator page is reachable from the inn network

title: Control assessment: Backup review
source_system: Innkeeping vendor SOC 2 report; laptop folders; file account settings; owner self-review
what_it_shows: Contracts, tax documents and receipts on the laptop have no backup and the innkeeping data has never been exported; security documents are kept only on the laptop; the innkeeping vendor backs up the system, encrypts backups, checks their integrity and keeps them in a separate location (SOC 2 report, no exceptions)

title: Control assessment: MFA sign-in test
source_system: Account security pages; sign-in tests from a new browser
what_it_shows: The innkeeping administrator account, email and OTA-2 signed in with a password only; the accounting SaaS and OTA-1 required a code sent to the owner's phone

title: Control assessment: Passwords and door codes test
source_system: Laptop browser password list; router login page; lock app code settings; owner self-review
what_it_shows: Vendors verify the owner's identity by email or phone when accounts are created or recovered; per-reservation door codes are random 6-digit codes; one password is reused for the innkeeping software and email and several are under 10 characters; 18 passwords are saved in the family laptop's browser; the router administrator sign-in succeeded with the default password printed on the device label; the house master code has not changed since 2022, including when a cleaner left in 2024; the relief innkeeper uses the owner's passwords; no procedure for a lost phone or compromised password, and no stored recovery codes; the phone passcode and encryption protect the sign-in codes and the payment app

title: Control assessment: Incident reporting self-review
source_system: Sub-merchant agreement; contact list (none); owner self-review
what_it_shows: No reporting time is set for the relief innkeeper; the owner did not know the facilitator's 24-hour notice term before intake; there is no list of whom to notify (payment facilitator, innkeeping vendor, OTAs, counsel, Florida Department of Legal Affairs)

title: Control assessment: Provider review and lock app account test
source_system: Vendor folder; AOCs; innkeeping vendor SOC 2 report; AI add-on settings; lock app user list
what_it_shows: No security requirements, provider list or oversight steps are documented; the AI add-on was switched on without its terms being read; the consumer email provider holds card forms and ID photos; the AI add-on keeps chat transcripts with no deletion date; the lock installer's administrator account in the lock app was still active from the 2022 installation, and the owner disabled it during the session; customer responsibilities are listed in the innkeeping vendor's SOC 2 report and both AOCs; the AOCs and SOC 2 report were first obtained on 2026-07-22 and no ongoing check is defined

title: Control assessment: Encryption status check
source_system: Laptop and phone encryption status screens; mailbox search results; vendor AOCs
what_it_shows: Laptop full-disk encryption off; phone encrypted; card numbers in clear text in about 85 emails; the vendors' vaults encrypt stored card numbers

title: Control assessment: Stored card data and retention review
source_system: Desk drawer; mailbox search; phone photo count; innkeeping register report; owner self-review
what_it_shows: Card numbers with security codes are kept on paper and in email; about 1,900 ID photos and all guest profiles since 2019 are kept with no retention rule; pad pages and printed card forms have never been destroyed; printed arrivals lists are shredded each week; the register report is available electronically for 2 years

title: Control assessment: Malicious code protection test
source_system: Antivirus status page; standard antivirus test file downloaded on the laptop
what_it_shows: The built-in antivirus detected the test file on download and quarantined it; signature updates install automatically (last update the same day); scheduled and real-time scans on; the alert was shown to the owner; no false positives recorded
